To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neither DM nor overweight is a risk factor for hepatocellular cancer.
neither DM nor overweight were shown to be significant risk factors for HCV or HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma in a dual HBsAg and anti-HCV endemic area.
in a dual HBsAg and anti-HCV endemic area, neither DM nor obesity was shown to be a risk factor for hepatocellular cancer, but male gender, age, HBsAg, and anti-HCV were independent risk factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of diabetes mellitus and overweight in hepatocellular carcinoma development in a dual hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C virus endemic area.
the roles of DM in HCC development and the roles of overweight in HCC progression.
the risk factors for HCV and HBV in a community-based study in southern Taiwan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk factors of HCC in a high-prevalence HBV and HAV endemic area are HBV and HCC, male gender, and age (≧65 years).
neither DM nor overweight should be considered as risk factors for HCV- or HBV-related HCC.
DM and overweight are not independent risk factors for the development of HCC in the dual HBV and anti-HCV endemic area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DM and overweight were not independent risk factors for the development of HCC in a community-based study in a dual HBsAg- and anti-HCV-endemic area.
HCC development is a multifactorial process, with HBV, HCV, and high ALT being the most important factors, and that DM and obesity are not independent risk factors.
HCC is a disease of the elderly with a history of HBV infection and/or chronic HCV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the roles of DM or overweight as risk factors for HCV-associated HCC are less important than those in HBV-associated HCC.
the roles of DM or obesity in HCC development are not significant in a community with a dual HBV-HCV endemic background.
the prevalence of diabetes in the general population is low, and diabetes is not a risk factor for the development of HCC.
